chunks: My father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khālid Al-Barqi, from Qāsim ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from his grandfather Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from Abū Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) who said:

When one leaves his house to go to the Ziyārah of Abī ‘Abdillāh, Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him), Allāh will dedicate an angel to him who will place his finger on the back of the Zā`ir and who will start writing every word which comes out of his mouth until he arrives at the Ḥā`ir. After he exits from the doors of the Ḥā`ir, the angel will place his palm on the middle of the back of the Zā`ir and say, “Surely all of your past sins have been forgiven. Therefore, continue with good deeds.” The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: from Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from Ibrāhīm ibn Abil Bilād, with the same chain.

key_terms.حَائِر: Ha'ir (a specific area near Mecca or the shrine)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of visiting the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh narrates that an angel accompanies the pilgrim to Karbala, continuously recording their utterances until they reach al-Ha'ir, the boundary of the sacred precincts. Upon crossing this threshold, the angel signifies the absolution of all prior sins, inviting the visitor to begin anew with a clean slate, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatology regarding the intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt.
